family: C-X vs per-target comparator on r2_anomaly, 2 blocks x 6 targets = 12 tests, Holm (alpha 0.05); p = two-sided paired location-cluster bootstrap p if delta > 0 else 1. v11 item 1: the per-target comparator is re-chosen among the enlarged listed set (X-L 16, X-U 19) by the unchanged §6 rule; any Holm family formed over listed comparators (events: derived vs each comparator) grows with the list; no denominator is held at its earlier size.
decision_table: Protocol §8 as amended by v9, v10 and v11; first matching row. 'Listed comparator' = every comparator in comparator_set of the block (X-L 16, X-U 19, the two rule comparators of v11 item 1 included); each is compared with C-X by the paired location-cluster bootstrap of r2_anomaly (B = 10,000, seed-mean predictions).
3* (v10, checked first) paired CI upper < 0 against ANY listed comparator -> Below

1 Holm-rejected & per-seed delta > 0 (seeds 0,1,2) & region-unit paired CI > 0 & paired CI lower > 0 against EVERY listed comparator (no finite estimate = not beaten) -> SOTA (M5-X, block, within-region)
2 Holm-rejected (row 1 not met) -> Above, not robust; the reason names each failed condition and each listed comparator not beaten
3 CI upper < 0 against the per-target comparator -> Below
4 CI includes 0 & realised Holm-worst MDE (3.71 * CI width / 3.92) > 0.02 -> Inconclusive (underpowered)
A family delta with no finite estimate -> Not estimable (reported, never a claim)

v11 item 6d: a confirmatory row in which a label-deciding quantity lies within the reproducibility tolerance of its threshold is flagged; the label stands. 6e: a bootstrap p of 0 is reported as '< 2/B'.
DISCLOSURE_POWER_TABLE_OPTIMISTIC_V11: Protocol v11 item 5: the registered power table (power_x; a proxy from NRSA Test A) is optimistic. The pre-test reviewer scaled the development paired CIs of C-X vs comparator to the test cluster counts: projected test SE 0.008-0.020 on X-L (registered 0.006-0.010) and 0.006-0.026 on X-U (registered 0.004-0.0065); projected Holm-worst detectable difference above 0.02 for all 12 targets (X-L 0.031-0.073, X-U 0.022-0.098). sota_expectation.definition: SOTA campaign (docs/plans/sota_campaign.md): expected outcome of the confirmatory candidate C-X per target on DEVELOPMENT (seed 0, paired location-cluster bootstrap B=2,000 of r2_anomaly): 'SOTA-expected' if the paired CI excludes 0 above vs BOTH the strongest published method (WA-PLS2, kNN-MAT, bio.infer, GJAM where its fidelity check passed) AND the strongest simple/practitioner baseline (region mean, RF[geography], nearest reference, UK-index regressions) AND the per-target comparator; 'negative' if below either; else 'competitive'. Development only — the label itself comes only from the single test look (§8).

reproducibility_rule: Protocol v11 item 6: runs are not bit-reproducible (two development dry runs of one record differed by up to 4.4e-5 in delta, 9.7e-5 in CI ends, 1.5e-4 in per-seed delta and 0.0016 in p). (a) The sealed predictions of the one look are the record and are never refitted. (b) A rescore from the same sealed predictions must reproduce every stored number within rescore_abs and every label exactly; otherwise both result sets are kept and no label is used until the lead has ruled. (c) A later refit from the snapshot (reproduction, never a second look) reproduces the result when delta and CI ends agree within delta / ci, per-seed delta within per_seed_delta and p within p. (d) Confirmatory rows within these tolerances of a label threshold are flagged. (e) A bootstrap p of 0 is reported as '< 2/B'.

The scorer refuses a record whose list differs from the protocol's or whose rule comparators do not follow from its own C-X. The confirmatory family stays 12 tests (C-X vs the per-target comparator, re-chosen among the enlarged list by the unchanged rule).

Comparators: strongest of all §6 comparators per (block, target) by development r2_anomaly, each in its chosen variant. Amendments v9/v10 change the scorer and the label rule only: no model was fitted or selected on development after them. Amendment v11 adds the two rule comparators (means of existing development predictions) and restructures the look; C-X, the secondaries, every model, feature set, seed, split and fold are unchanged and no model was fitted on development for it.
freeze_procedure: After the independent pre-test review, the LEAD writes docs/preregistration/bioassess_x_freeze.json = this record with status 'frozen', frozen_at and candidate_sha256 = sha256 of this file. The scorer accepts only that file (xtestlook.load_freeze) and never this candidate. The look is started from the code snapshot in code_snapshot.dir (python -B <dir>/scripts/eval/bioassess_x_final.py); every command verifies the snapshot's exact file set and hashes and refuses in real mode from any other tree. The freeze file, this candidate and the registry stay in the live repository (v11 item 3).
resume_rule: Protocol v11 item 2 (replaces the single-resume rule of §9, v5 and v7b). Four commands: claim, chunk, seal, score. Prediction phase: label-free; one write-once unit per (block, leaf model, fold, seed) and per event fit, each with its own file and sha256; chunks may run in any order, in parallel, and be started again any number of times before sealing; each chunk re-verifies the freeze record, the code snapshot, the data pins and the artifacts; a failed or killed chunk leaves finished units in place and does not end the look. The seal is written once, when every planned unit exists and verifies. Scoring is single-shot and is not resumed: if it stops before the one locked registry write, --rescore-from-saved recomputes everything from the sealed predictions (recorded; agreement within rescore_abs required where the stopped run left results); once the scoring rows exist, no scoring run can write again.
test_rows_note: test rows are loaded with the design rules of xdata (NLA: first visit with benthic taxa; UK: >= 3 harmonised taxa); the numbers loaded vs in the split table are recorded in pass_info.json. Correction (v11 item 4a): 459 of the 974 X-L test rows lie at Fuse/D2n test sites (439 Fuse tier-C, 20 more D2n-only), not 549 as §2 said; counts from sample keys only.

defects_found_and_fixed: A unit whose fit raised killed the whole chunk and every later chunk failed on the same unit, so the look could not reach the seal (seen on bio.infer with a capped training set). Fixed: the chunk records the failing unit, writes nothing for it, goes on to the next one and ends with exit 6 naming it; a later chunk fits it again, and nothing unfitted can be sealed. Unit-tested.

The rehearsal cap starved bio.infer's R code (mlsolve could not build its coefficient matrix). Fixed: the R methods get R_CAP_FACTOR = 3 times the cap in the dry run (they are not the expensive unit), the cap itself is still refused in real mode. Unit-tested.

The whole prediction phase took 28 min with one GPU chunk and one CPU chunk at the cap; the scoring step took 1 h 40 min by itself and is the item to schedule, not the fits.
The GPU chunk queues on the shared sentinel GPU lock and starts when a permitted GPU frees; it does not take a GPU another job holds.
